question: Under Rule A.0110(c), a licensed real estate firm is NOT required to designate a BIC if it meets which set of conditions?
choice_a: It is organized solely to receive compensation for brokerage services furnished by its qualifying broker through another firm or broker, is treated as a pass-through entity for federal tax purposes, has no principal or branch office, and has no licensed person associated with it other than its qualifying broker
choice_b: It has fewer than five affiliated brokers
choice_c: It has been in business for less than one year
choice_d: It operates only online with no physical signage
explanation: Rule A.0110(c) exempts a firm from the BIC requirement only if it is organized solely to receive pass-through compensation for its qualifying broker's services through another firm or broker, is IRS pass-through for tax purposes, has no principal or branch office, and has no licensed person associated with it other than its qualifying broker.
source_note: Broker-In-Charge, Firms Not Required to Have a BIC [Rule A.0110(c)]

question: Under Rule A.0110(e)(6)(C), when must the 12-hour Broker-in-Charge Course be completed relative to a broker's application for BIC Eligible status?
choice_a: No earlier than one year prior to the application and no later than 120 days after the application
choice_b: At any time during the broker's career, with no window restriction
choice_c: Only within 30 days before the application is filed
choice_d: Only after the Commission approves the application
explanation: The BIC Eligible status application requires certification that the broker completed the 12-hour Broker-in-Charge Course no earlier than one year prior to the application and no later than 120 days after the application.
source_note: Broker-In-Charge, Application for BIC Eligible Status [Rule A.0110(e)(6)(C)]

question: Under Rule A.0110(g)(1), a designated BIC must assure that each broker affiliated at the office has complied with which Commission rules?
choice_a: Rules .0503, .0504, and .0506 - governing license renewal, active license status, and provisional broker supervision
choice_b: Only the advertising rules
choice_c: Only the fair housing rules
choice_d: There is no such requirement placed on the BIC
explanation: Rule A.0110(g)(1) requires a designated BIC to assure that each broker affiliated at the office has complied with Rules .0503, .0504, and .0506 of the Subchapter.

question: Which of the following is a duty a broker-in-charge owes to the Commission regarding the firm itself, distinct from an individual broker's personal duty under Rule A.0103?
choice_a: Notifying the Commission of any change in the firm's business address or trade name, and the registration of any assumed business name adopted by the firm
choice_b: Filing the firm's federal tax return with the Commission
choice_c: Approving every affiliated broker's personal vacation requests
choice_d: There is no firm-level notification duty placed on the BIC
explanation: Rule A.0110(g)(2) requires a BIC to notify the Commission of any change of the firm's business address or trade name, and of the registration of any assumed business name adopted by the firm for its use.

question: Under Rule A.0110(g)(3), who is responsible for the conduct of advertising placed by or in the name of a real estate firm at a given office?
choice_a: The broker-in-charge of that office
choice_b: Any affiliated broker who happens to author the ad, with no BIC involvement
choice_c: The Real Estate Commission itself
choice_d: No one - advertising is unregulated at the firm level
explanation: Rule A.0110(g)(3) makes the designated BIC responsible for the conduct of advertising by or in the name of the firm at that office.

question: Under Rule A.0110(g)(4), which of the following is an explicit duty of the designated BIC?
choice_a: Maintaining the trust or escrow account of the firm and the records pertaining to it
choice_b: Personally negotiating every offer for all affiliated brokers
choice_c: Setting the commission split for every listing in the office
choice_d: Approving the firm's marketing budget
explanation: Rule A.0110(g)(4) requires the designated BIC to maintain the trust or escrow account of the firm and the records pertaining to it.

question: Rule A.0110(g)(6) requires a designated BIC to supervise which category of licensees associated with or engaged on behalf of the firm at that office?
choice_a: Provisional brokers, in accordance with the requirements of Rule A.0506
choice_b: Only brokers who have been licensed more than ten years
choice_c: Only brokers who already hold BIC Eligible status themselves
choice_d: Unlicensed clerical staff only
explanation: Rule A.0110(g)(6) requires the BIC to supervise provisional brokers associated with or engaged on behalf of the firm at that office, in accordance with Rule A.0506.

question: Under Rule A.0110(g)(7), a BIC must supervise all brokers affiliated at the office with respect to adherence to which requirements?
choice_a: Agency agreement and disclosure requirements
choice_b: Personal income tax withholding elections
choice_c: Continuing legal education requirements for attorneys
choice_d: Local zoning compliance for every listed property
explanation: Rule A.0110(g)(7) requires the BIC to supervise all brokers affiliated at the office with respect to their adherence to agency agreement and disclosure requirements.

question: Under Rule A.0110(g)(9), within how many days of assuming responsibility for a trust account must a BIC complete the Commission's Basic Trust Account Procedures Course, and how often is it required at most?
choice_a: Within 120 days of assuming responsibility, but no more than once in any three-year period
choice_b: Within 10 days, and every single year without exception
choice_c: There is no deadline to complete this course
choice_d: Within one year, and only once in a broker's entire career regardless of gaps in service
explanation: Rule A.0110(g)(9) requires a BIC to complete the Commission's Basic Trust Account Procedures Course within 120 days of assuming responsibility for a trust account per G.S. 93A-6(g), but the BIC need not complete the course more than once in three years.
source_note: Broker-In-Charge, Duties of BIC [Rule A.0110(g)(9); G.S. 93A-6(g)]

question: Under Rule A.0110(g)(10), a BIC's supervisory duty extends to which additional group at the office, beyond licensed brokers?
choice_a: Unlicensed individuals employed at the office, to ensure their activities comply with G.S. 93A-2(c)(6)
choice_b: Only the firm's outside accountant
choice_c: Customers who visit the office
choice_d: There is no duty to supervise unlicensed staff
explanation: Rule A.0110(g)(10) requires a BIC to supervise all unlicensed individuals employed at the office and ensure that they comply with G.S. 93A-2(c)(6).

question: Under Rule A.0110(h), when must a broker holding BIC Eligible status take the Broker-in-Charge Update Course, absent an exception?
choice_a: During the license year of designation, unless the broker has already satisfied the requirements of Rule .1702 prior to designation
choice_b: Only in the broker's final year before retirement
choice_c: Within 24 hours of designation
choice_d: There is no timing requirement for this course
explanation: Rule A.0110(h) requires a broker holding BIC Eligible status to take the Broker-in-Charge Update Course during the license year of designation, unless the requirements of Rule .1702 were already satisfied prior to designation.
source_note: Broker-In-Charge, Maintaining BIC Eligible Status [Rule A.0110(h)]

question: Under Rule A.0110(i), which of the following will cause a broker's BIC Eligible status to terminate?
choice_a: Making any false statements or presenting false, incomplete, or incorrect information in connection with a BIC Eligible status application
choice_b: Taking a scheduled vacation during the license year
choice_c: Working part-time instead of full-time as a broker
choice_d: Changing firms without changing office locations
explanation: Rule A.0110(i)(1) provides that a broker's BIC Eligible status terminates if the broker made any false statements or presented false, incomplete, or incorrect information in connection with an application.
source_note: Broker-In-Charge, Termination of BIC Eligible Status [Rule A.0110(i)]

question: Besides failing required coursework, what other event under Rule A.0110(i) causes a broker's BIC Eligible status to terminate?
choice_a: Failure to timely renew the broker license, or the license being suspended, revoked, or surrendered
choice_b: Moving to a new residence within the same county
choice_c: Hiring a new unlicensed assistant
choice_d: Completing an elective CE course beyond what is required
explanation: Rule A.0110(i)(3) provides that BIC Eligible status terminates if the broker fails to renew his or her broker license, or the license has been suspended, revoked, or surrendered.
source_note: Broker-In-Charge, Termination of BIC Eligible Status [Rule A.0110(i)]

question: May a nonresident commercial real estate broker licensed under Section .1800 serve as broker-in-charge of a firm or office in North Carolina?
choice_a: No - Rule A.0110(k) prohibits a nonresident commercial real estate broker from acting as or serving in the capacity of a BIC in North Carolina
choice_b: Yes, without restriction
choice_c: Yes, but only for commercial (not residential) offices
choice_d: Yes, as long as they complete the 12-hour BIC Course
explanation: Rule A.0110(k) provides that a nonresident commercial real estate broker licensed under Section .1800 of the Subchapter shall not act as or serve in the capacity of a BIC of a firm or office in North Carolina.

question: Under Rule A.0110(l), may a broker be granted BIC Eligible status or designated as a firm's BIC while there is a pending Commission investigation against that broker?
choice_a: No - a broker shall not be granted BIC Eligible status or designated as BIC of a firm if there is a pending Commission investigation against the broker
choice_b: Yes, pending investigations have no bearing on BIC status
choice_c: Yes, but only if the investigation has been open for more than a year
choice_d: Only the Executive Director may waive this restriction, and does so routinely
explanation: Rule A.0110(l) bars a broker from being granted BIC Eligible status or designated as BIC of a firm if there is a pending Commission investigation against the broker.

question: As a general rule under Rule A.0506(a), by how many brokers-in-charge may a provisional broker be supervised at one time?
choice_a: Only one, except for a narrow co-listing/co-selling exception involving two affiliated firms in the same physical location
choice_b: As many as the provisional broker chooses to affiliate with
choice_c: Exactly two, always
choice_d: None - provisional brokers are self-supervising after their first year of licensure
explanation: Rule A.0506(a) provides that a provisional broker shall be supervised by only one broker-in-charge at a time, except that the provisional broker may be supervised by no more than two BICs of two licensed affiliated firms located in the same physical location acting as co-listing or co-selling agents.

question: Under Rule A.0506(a), when a provisional broker is supervised by two brokers-in-charge under the co-listing/co-selling exception, how is supervisory responsibility allocated between them?
choice_a: Both brokers-in-charge bear all supervision responsibility at all times
choice_b: Only the BIC who introduced the provisional broker to the firm bears any responsibility
choice_c: Responsibility is split 50/50 and each BIC is liable only for half of any violation
choice_d: Neither BIC bears responsibility once a second BIC is added
explanation: Rule A.0506(a) provides that when a provisional broker is supervised by more than one broker-in-charge under the narrow co-listing/co-selling exception, both brokers-in-charge bear all supervision responsibility at all times.

question: Upon a provisional broker's affiliation with a real estate firm, who must file the License Activation and Broker Affiliation form with the Commission?
choice_a: The broker-in-charge of the office where the provisional broker will be engaged in the real estate business
choice_b: The provisional broker's spouse or next of kin
choice_c: The Commission itself, automatically upon licensure
choice_d: The provisional broker's prelicensing school
explanation: Rule A.0506(b) requires the broker-in-charge of the office where the provisional broker will be engaged in business to file the License Activation and Broker Affiliation form with the Commission.

question: Under Rule A.0506(c), what must a provisional broker do if he or she and the BIC do not receive written acknowledgment from the Commission within 30 days of the License Activation and Broker Affiliation form's date?
choice_a: Cease all real estate brokerage activities pending receipt of the written acknowledgment from the Commission
choice_b: Continue working normally, since the 30-day period is only a guideline
choice_c: File suit against the Commission for the delay
choice_d: Automatically be treated as a fully licensed broker
explanation: Rule A.0506(c) requires the provisional broker to cease all real estate brokerage activities if written acknowledgment from the Commission is not received within 30 days of the date on the form, pending receipt of that acknowledgment.

question: Under Rule A.0506(d), what may happen to a broker-in-charge who fails to supervise a provisional broker as the rule prescribes?
choice_a: The BIC may be subject to disciplinary action pursuant to Rule A.0110
choice_b: Nothing - only the provisional broker can ever be disciplined for supervision lapses
choice_c: The BIC's license is automatically revoked with no hearing
choice_d: The firm must close its doors within 24 hours
explanation: Rule A.0506(d) requires a BIC to supervise a provisional broker in a manner that assures compliance with License Law and Commission rules; a supervising broker who fails to do so may be subject to disciplinary action under Rule A.0110.

question: Upon termination of the supervisory relationship between a provisional broker and BIC, within how many days must written notification of the termination date be provided to the Commission?
choice_a: 10 days
choice_b: 30 days
choice_c: 60 days
choice_d: There is no notification requirement
explanation: Rule A.0506(e) requires the provisional broker and the broker-in-charge to provide written notification of the termination date to the Commission not later than 10 days following the termination of their supervisory relationship.

question: Under Rule A.0120(b), from whom may an affiliated broker be paid a commission or referral fee directly?
choice_a: Only their current BIC, or the person who served as their BIC at the time of the transaction
choice_b: Any brokerage firm operating in the state
choice_c: The buyer or seller directly, bypassing the firm entirely
choice_d: Any licensed appraiser involved in the deal
explanation: Rule A.0120(b) provides that an affiliated broker shall not be paid a commission or referral fee directly by anyone other than their current BIC or the person who served as their BIC at the time of the transaction.

question: Under Rule A.0120(c), which of the following is prohibited?
choice_a: A broker coercing, extorting, colluding with, instructing, inducing, bribing, or intimidating a service provider - such as an appraiser, attorney, inspector, lender, or contractor - to influence their findings, report, or decision
choice_b: A broker recommending a qualified service provider to a client
choice_c: A broker attending a real estate closing
choice_d: A broker requesting a repair estimate from a contractor
explanation: Rule A.0120(c) prohibits a broker from coercing, extorting, colluding with, instructing, inducing, bribing, or intimidating a service provider in a real estate transaction to influence or attempt to influence their findings, report, or decision.

question: Under Rule A.0120(d), a broker shall not conduct brokerage activities or promote their status as a broker in a manner that discriminates on which bases?
choice_a: Race, color, religion, national origin, sex, familial status, or disability
choice_b: Only religion
choice_c: Only national origin and sex
choice_d: The rule does not list any protected characteristics
explanation: Rule A.0120(d) prohibits a broker from conducting brokerage activities or otherwise promoting their status as a broker in any manner that discriminates on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, familial status, or disability.

question: Under Rule A.0109(c)(1), in a real estate sales transaction, compensation of more than nominal value from a broker's own principal is only permissible if:
choice_a: It is provided for in a written agency contract prepared in conformity with the requirements of Rule A.0104
choice_b: The broker mentions it verbally one time
choice_c: The Commission pre-approves the specific dollar amount
choice_d: It is paid entirely in cash
explanation: Rule A.0109(c)(1) provides that in a sales transaction, a broker shall not receive compensation of more than nominal value from his or her principal unless it is provided for in a written agency contract prepared in conformity with Rule A.0104.

question: Under Rule A.0109(d), what must 'full disclosure' of compensation include?
choice_a: A description of the compensation, incentive, bonus, or rebate, including its value and the identity of the person or party by whom it will or may be paid
choice_b: Only the broker's signature on a blank form
choice_c: A verbal acknowledgment with no further specifics
choice_d: The broker's personal Social Security number
explanation: Rule A.0109(d) defines full disclosure as including a description of the compensation, incentive, bonus, rebate, or other consideration, including its value and the identity of the person or party by whom it will or may be paid.
source_note: Brokerage Fees and Compensation, Full and Timely Disclosure [Rule A.0109(d)]

question: Under Rule A.0109(d), a disclosure of compensation is considered 'timely' when it is made:
choice_a: In sufficient time to aid a reasonable person's decision-making
choice_b: Within exactly 24 hours of closing, and never before
choice_c: Only after the transaction has already closed
choice_d: Whenever the broker personally finds it convenient
explanation: Rule A.0109(d) provides that a disclosure is timely when it is made in sufficient time to aid a reasonable person's decision-making.
source_note: Brokerage Fees and Compensation, Full and Timely Disclosure [Rule A.0109(d)]

question: Under Rule A.0109(e), which disclosure is a broker NOT required to make?
choice_a: Disclosing to a person who is not the broker's principal the compensation the broker expects to receive from the broker's own principal, or disclosing to the principal the compensation the broker expects from the broker's employing broker
choice_b: Disclosing a referral fee received for recommending a home inspector to a client
choice_c: Disclosing a $5,000 bonus offered by a homebuilder for steering buyers to its development
choice_d: Disclosing any compensation whatsoever, under any circumstance
explanation: Rule A.0109(e) clarifies that nothing in the rule requires a broker to disclose to a non-principal the compensation expected from the broker's own principal, or to disclose to the principal the compensation expected from the broker's employing broker.

question: Under Rule A.0109(g), except for the narrow travel agent exception in paragraph (h), a licensee shall not undertake what course of conduct?
choice_a: Any arrangement, contract, plan, or other course of conduct to compensate or share compensation with unlicensed persons or entities for acts performed in North Carolina requiring licensure
choice_b: Advertising the same listing on more than one website
choice_c: Holding an open house without the seller physically present
choice_d: Referring a client to another licensed broker
explanation: Rule A.0109(g) prohibits a licensee, except as provided in the travel agent exception of paragraph (h), from undertaking any arrangement, contract, plan, or other course of conduct to compensate or share compensation with unlicensed persons or entities for acts requiring licensure performed in North Carolina.

question: Under Rule A.0109(h), when must payments to a travel agent for procuring a vacation rental tenant be made, and what must the broker provide the tenant before a binding agreement is created?
choice_a: Payment only after conclusion of the vacation rental tenancy; the broker must give the tenant a written statement advising reliance only on the rental agreement and the broker's representations
choice_b: Payment upfront before any tenant is found, with no disclosure required to the tenant
choice_c: Payment monthly throughout the tenancy, with no written statement required
choice_d: There is no timing restriction on when payment may be made
explanation: Rule A.0109(h) requires that payments to a travel agent be made only after conclusion of the vacation rental tenancy, and that the broker provide the introduced tenant a written statement, prior to creation of a binding agreement, advising reliance only on the agreement and the broker's representations.
source_note: Brokerage Fees and Compensation, Travel Agent Exception [Rule A.0109(h)]

question: Does Rule A.0109 permit a licensee to accept a fee or kickback that is otherwise prohibited by the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (RESPA)?
choice_a: No - Rule A.0109(i) states nothing in the rule shall be construed to permit acceptance of any fee, kickback, or other valuable consideration prohibited by RESPA or HUD regulations
choice_b: Yes, state real estate rules override federal RESPA restrictions
choice_c: Yes, as long as the broker's principal consents in writing
choice_d: Only in commercial transactions is RESPA inapplicable
explanation: Rule A.0109(i) clarifies that nothing in the rule permits a licensee to accept any fee, kickback, or other valuable consideration prohibited by RESPA (12 U.S.C. 2601 et seq.) or its implementing HUD regulations, or to skip any disclosure RESPA requires.

question: Under G.S. 93A-6(a)(5), from whom may a provisional broker accept a commission or valuable consideration for performing real estate brokerage acts?
choice_a: Only from his or her broker-in-charge or the licensed broker by whom he or she is employed
choice_b: From any buyer or seller directly, without restriction
choice_c: From any licensed broker in the state, regardless of employer
choice_d: From an unlicensed referral source who found the client
explanation: G.S. 93A-6(a)(5) makes it disciplinable for a provisional broker to accept a commission or valuable consideration for brokerage acts from any person except his or her broker-in-charge or the licensed broker by whom he or she is employed.

question: Under G.S. 93A-6(a)(6), a licensee may be disciplined for:
choice_a: Representing or attempting to represent a real estate broker other than the broker by whom he or she is engaged or associated, without that broker's express knowledge and consent
choice_b: Attending a real estate industry conference
choice_c: Listing the same property in more than one MLS
choice_d: Referring a buyer to a mortgage lender
explanation: G.S. 93A-6(a)(6) makes it disciplinable to represent or attempt to represent a real estate broker other than the broker by whom the licensee is engaged or associated, without the express knowledge and consent of the broker with whom he or she is associated.

question: Under G.S. 93A-6(a)(7), a licensee may be disciplined for failing to do what within a reasonable time?
choice_a: Account for or remit any monies coming into his or her possession which belong to others
choice_b: Attend a continuing education course
choice_c: Return every client phone call
choice_d: Renew a driver's license
explanation: G.S. 93A-6(a)(7) makes it disciplinable to fail, within a reasonable time, to account for or to remit any monies coming into a licensee's possession which belong to others.

question: G.S. 93A-6(a)(8) authorizes discipline for a licensee found to be:
choice_a: Unworthy or incompetent to act as a real estate broker in a manner as to endanger the interest of the public
choice_b: Late to a single scheduled showing appointment
choice_c: A member of more than one professional real estate association
choice_d: Working more than 40 hours per week
explanation: G.S. 93A-6(a)(8) authorizes discipline for a licensee who is unworthy or incompetent to act as a real estate broker in a manner as to endanger the interest of the public.

question: Under G.S. 93A-6(a)(9), a licensee may be disciplined for:
choice_a: Paying a commission or valuable consideration to any person for acts or services performed in violation of Chapter 93A
choice_b: Paying a commission to a fully licensed, active broker for a completed transaction
choice_c: Paying a referral fee that falls within the narrow travel-agent exception under Rule A.0109(h)
choice_d: Receiving a commission from a client at closing
explanation: G.S. 93A-6(a)(9) makes it disciplinable to pay a commission or valuable consideration to any person for acts or services performed in violation of Chapter 93A - this is the statutory anchor for the rule against compensating unlicensed persons.

question: Under G.S. 93A-6(a)(15), what constitutes an independent ground for Commission discipline?
choice_a: Violating any rule adopted by the Commission
choice_b: Violating only a statute, never a Commission rule
choice_c: Nothing - Commission rules are unenforceable without a matching statutory violation
choice_d: Only violations that were reported by another licensed broker
explanation: G.S. 93A-6(a)(15) makes violating any rule adopted by the Commission, standing alone, a ground for disciplinary action.

question: Under G.S. 93A-6(b)(3), the Commission may discipline a licensee who violates the provisions of G.S. 93A-6(a) in what context?
choice_a: When selling, leasing, or buying the licensee's own property
choice_b: Only when representing a corporate client
choice_c: Only in transactions involving commercial property
choice_d: This subsection places no additional context on G.S. 93A-6(a)
explanation: G.S. 93A-6(b)(3) allows discipline when a licensee has violated any of the provisions of G.S. 93A-6(a) when selling, leasing, or buying the licensee's own property - the same misconduct standards apply even to a broker's personal real estate dealings.

question: Under G.S. 93A-6(b)(4), when can a broker be disciplined for the acts of an unlicensed employee who is exempt from licensure under G.S. 93A-2(c)(6)?
choice_a: When that unlicensed employee, in the regular course of business, commits an act that would constitute a violation of G.S. 93A-6(a) if committed by the broker
choice_b: Never - an unlicensed employee's acts can never be attributed to the broker
choice_c: Only if the broker personally witnessed the unlicensed employee's act
choice_d: Only if the unlicensed employee is a member of the broker's immediate family
explanation: G.S. 93A-6(b)(4) allows discipline of a broker when the broker's unlicensed employee - exempt under G.S. 93A-2(c)(6) - has committed, in the regular course of business, an act that would constitute a G.S. 93A-6(a) violation if committed by the broker.

question: Under G.S. 93A-6(e), when a licensee is accused of misconduct that would subject them to discipline, what alternative may they pursue with the Commission's consent and approval?
choice_a: Surrender the license and all related rights and privileges for a period of time set by the Commission, during which they may not apply for real estate licensure
choice_b: Pay a fine and continue practicing with no further restriction
choice_c: Transfer the license to another qualified individual
choice_d: Demand a jury trial in place of a Commission hearing
explanation: G.S. 93A-6(e) allows a licensee accused of misconduct, with Commission consent and approval, to surrender the license and all rights and privileges pertaining to it for a period established by the Commission; the licensee may not apply for licensure during the surrender period.
source_note: Disciplinary Action by Commission, License Surrender [G.S. 93A-6(e)]

question: Under G.S. 93A-6(g), a broker's trust or escrow account shall be what type of account?
choice_a: A demand deposit account in a federally insured depository institution lawfully doing business in North Carolina that agrees to make its records of the account available for inspection by the Commission
choice_b: Any interest-bearing certificate of deposit chosen by the broker
choice_c: A personal savings account held in the broker's own name
choice_d: An out-of-state account not subject to Commission inspection
explanation: G.S. 93A-6(g) requires a broker's trust or escrow account to be a demand deposit account in a federally insured depository institution lawfully doing business in North Carolina that agrees to make its account records available for inspection by the Commission's representatives.

question: When applying for BIC Eligible status, a broker must certify compliance with which statute regarding active license status and brokerage experience?
explanation: Rule A.0110(e)(6) requires a BIC Eligible status applicant to certify compliance with G.S. 93A-4.2, including that the broker's license is on active status and the broker has the requisite brokerage experience or attorney-practice equivalent.
source_note: Broker-In-Charge, Application for BIC Eligible Status [Rule A.0110(e)(6); G.S. 93A-4.2]
